finite_default_domain.scope: Default native parameter distribution only; finite input count is not inflated by repeated sampling.

provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The colours are taken from the palette as constants: background = palette[0], frame = palette[5], liquid = palette[8]. The emitted program works directly in the visible grid. It finds the bounding box of the frame-coloured cells and fills every background cell strictly inside it with the liquid colour. It then looks for the single background cell on the box border; that is the gap. The side of the box the gap sits on (top, bottom, left or right) sets the ray direction: up, down, left or right. The gap and every cell beyond it, up to the grid edge, are filled with liquid. Because the gap's side is read from the pixels, any rotation or reflection is handled without normalisation wrappers. The d4 value therefore needs no special handling. The generator always places the gap at a non-corner cell of one side, so the side and direction are always unambiguous.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes a single frame with exactly one border gap, as the generator always produces. If the palette background or frame colour is missing from the grid, the program falls back to the most common colour and the largest component. That path is not expected inside the domain. The test fixture's ray runs rightward, so it is a different orientation from the training pairs; the visible mechanism handles it all the same. I found no constructor defects or contradictions between the fixtures and the rule. Not tested by me.

independent_source_review.mechanism: Single gray (palette[5]) rectangular frame with exactly one background gap at a non-corner cell of one side. The solver takes the bounding box of the frame-coloured cells and fills every background cell strictly inside it with palette[8]. It then finds the single background cell on the box border; that is the gap. It colours the gap and casts a ray outward to the grid edge, choosing the direction from the side the gap is on (top→up, bottom→down, left→left, right→right).
evidence: Constructor before gravity: frame rows gap..gap+depth-1 and columns 2..size-3 (2..7). The top row is full. The bottom row skips c=5, so the gap is always a non-corner cell (5 lies strictly inside columns 2..7). The side columns span the full depth, so the bounding box of the frame colour equals the frame box.

The output colours interior rows gap+1..gap+depth-2 and columns 3..6 cyan, plus column 5 from the bottom row to size-1. That is exactly interior + gap + outward ray. No other non-background content exists, so every ray cell is background and nothing is overwritten.

gap ≤ size-depth-2 puts the bottom row at row ≤7, so the ray always has ≥2 cells beyond the frame. Under gravity 2 the frame can touch row 9 only on the side away from the gap, so the bounding box is unaffected.

common.apply_gravity was checked against common.py. gravity<2 means no flip; gravity≥2 means a vertical flip. gravity%2==1 means a transpose. The four resulting gap sides are bottom (0), right (1), top (2) and left (3); in each, the gap is still a unique non-corner border cell.

Fixtures are reproduced by validate parameters, with the train order swapped relative to validate. Train fixture 1 = (depth 5, gap 0, gravity 2): rows 5–9, top gap (5,5). Train fixture 2 = (depth 6, gap 2, gravity 0): rows 2–7, bottom gap (7,5). Test = (depth 5, gap 2, gravity 1): rows 2–7, columns 2–6, right gap (5,6).

The emitted solver works directly in visible coordinates. Direction comes from the gap's position on the bounding box, with no untransform/retransform wrapper. Specialising the colour constants bg/frame/fill from the palette is legitimate, and the demos teach fill=8.

The host audit passed: 1000 fresh pairs, 8000 augmented checks and 16 fixture variants. unique_base_inputs=28 matches the full latent space: depth 5 allows 4 gap offsets and depth 6 allows 3, giving 7 × 4 gravities.
nonblocking_limits: The generator's latent space is tiny (28 distinct base inputs). The frame width is always 6, the gap is always at the frame's central-ish column, and there is always exactly one frame. The audit therefore covers the domain exhaustively but says nothing about broader variants.
The fallback paths (missing palette bg/frame colour → most common colour / largest component; no gap → return unchanged) cannot be reached inside the constructor's domain.

The solver uses the bounding box of all frame-coloured cells, whereas the archived program uses the largest component. These are equivalent here only because the frame is the sole non-background object.
The gap search takes the first border background cell. This is unambiguous only because the constructor guarantees exactly one.
required_context_checks: None for colour association: d4f3cd78 is not on the episode-evidence list. Fill colour 8 is shown in every demonstration, and the direction is intrinsic to the gap's position, so D4 variants cannot produce conflicting query answers.
